reconcile.note: Gill answers that Matthew names both animals because Jesus actually rode each one in succession, so the accounts describe the same event.

discrepancy.note: Strauss singles out Matthew's two-animal detail as the account's most striking feature and rejects the harmonizers' readings that soften it.

quotes.text: This having been done, the disciples spread their clothes, and placed Jesus—on both the animals, according to Matthew; according to the two other synoptists, on the single animal.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §110, on Matthew 21:2 and Mark 11:2.

sides.snippet: you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Untie them, and bring them to me.
sides.verseText: saying to them, \"Go into the village that is opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied, and a colt with her. Untie them, and bring them to me.

sides.snippet: you will find a young donkey tied, on which no one has sat. Untie him, and bring him.
sides.verseText: and said to them, \"Go your way into the village that is opposite you. Immediately as you enter into it, you will find a young donkey tied, on which no one has sat. Untie him, and bring him.
